reference.name: Sunaga1995
reference.title: Chronopharmacology of enalapril in hypertensive patients.
reference.abstract: The pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of enalapril, an angiotensin converting enzyme inhibitor, are reported to vary with the time of administration. The present study was undertaken to examine whether the effect of enalapril on plasma bradykinin (BK), substance P and prostaglandin E2 (PGE2), which are likely to be involved in the mechanism of enalapril-induced cough, might also be affected by its time of administration. Enalapril 5 mg or placebo was given orally at 10:00 h (day trial) or 22:00 h (night trial) to 12 patients with essential hypertension. Serum concentrations of total drug (enalapril + enalaprilat, its active metabolite) during the day and night trials did not differ significantly at any time. However, serum enalaprilat tended to be higher and its maximum concentration greater in the day trial than in the night trial. Blood pressure 24 h after administration of enalapril was reduced at 22:00 h, but not at 10:00 h. Plasma BK tended to increase following enalapril administration at 10:00 h, but not at 22:00 h. Remarkable increases in plasma BK were observed in two patients in the day trial and one of them also complained of cough. However, no such increase in plasma BK or subsequent adverse effect were recorded in the night trial. Plasma substance P and PGE2 did not change significantly following enalapril administration either in the day or night trial. The results suggest that the response of BK to enalapril is affected by the time of administration. In patients who complain of cough during treatment with enalapril during the daytime, this adverse effect might be diminished or eliminated by a switch to night-time administration.

descriptions.text: Twelve inpatients (7 men and 5 women) with essential hypertension; Hypertension was defined as a diastolic BP > 90 mm Hg in the office
mean age was 45 y (range 25-61 y) and mean body weight was 63 kg (range 50 76 kg)
Enalapril maleate tablets 5 mg and placebo were used
Group I (n = 6) received placebo at 10:00 h and Day 1, enalapril at 10:00 h on Day 4, placebo at 22:00 h on Day 12 and enalapril at 22:00 h on Day 15
Group II (n = 6) received placebo at 22:00 h on Day 1, enalapril at 22:00 h on Day 4, placebo at 10:00 h on Day 12 and enalapril at 10:00 h on Day 15
Blood samples for determination of the serum drug concentration were obtained just before and 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 h
Blood samples taken before and 4 and 8 h after dosing were also used for deter- mination of plasma renin activity (PRA), and plasma concentrations of BK, substance P and PGE2
Systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) BP were measured before and 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 h
